current_text.html: An appellant shall be considered to have abandoned his appeal if he fails to appear before the higher court, in person or by counsel, for a hearing thereof, after he has been properly notified; but an appellant may waive, in writing, his right to appear with permission of the court and not be considered to have abandoned his case. In case of such failure to appear, the judgment of the lower court will stand unless the appellant gives to the court a prompt and satisfactory explanation.

relationships.title: Definition of 'appearance' before an adjudicating commission under BCO 42-11

metadata.summary: The CCB defined 'appearance' as the personal presence of a party or counsel before the adjudicating body after that body has given reasonable notice.

metadata.synopsis: Michael McNeil’s complaint against Chesapeake Presbytery was dismissed without a merits ruling after McNeil failed to appear at the SJC hearing. The panel called his name outside the hearing room and the Stated Clerk’s office; he was absent and had filed no brief. The notice had warned under BCO 42-11 that an appellant’s failure to appear would be treated as abandonment. The SJC declared the case abandoned and dismissed it. This illustrates dismissal for nonappearance, not adjudication of the underlying complaint.
